title: 31 August 1962: Live: Town Hall, Lydney
content:
The Beatles played two shows on consecutive nights in Gloucestershire on this and the following night. This first show took place at the Town Hall on Church Road in the town of Lydney.

The shows were promoted by Jaybee Clubs, run by John (Jack) Fallon and Bill Reid, who promoted events in a number of venues across the south of England. The Beatles played at four different Jaybee venues altogether.

The following night The Beatles performed for the second time at the Subscriptions Rooms in Stroud.

Page last updated: 25 January 2024

  • 2001: Ringo Starr and his All-Starr Band live: Concord Pavilion, Concord
  • 1973: Mixing: Meat City by John Lennon
  • 1969: Lennon, Harrison and Starr watch Bob Dylan perform at the Isle of Wight Festival
  • 1967: The Beatles meditate with Maharishi Mahesh Yogi in London
  • 1967: The Beatles issue a statement on NEMS Enterprises
  • 1965: The Beatles live: Cow Palace, San Francisco
  • 1964: Day off in Cape May, New Jersey
  • 1963: The Beatles live: Odeon Cinema, Southport
  • 1961: The Beatles live: St John’s Hall, Liverpool
  • 1960: The Beatles live: Indra Club, Hamburg
